text:
Theo: hey team, theo checking in first day on runtime. trying to build and run unit tests inside WSL2 on Win11 with CUDA 11.8 (WSL cuda toolkit) and docker+gpu passthrough. build fails at ptxas with unsupported PTX then later a cuDNN ABI mismatch. any WSL tips?
Theo: error snippet:
```
ptxas fatal : ValueError: unsupported PTX version '8.7'
/usr/bin/ld: warning: libcusolver.so.11, needed by ... not found
E0623 10:12:45.123456 12345 runtime.cc:123] cuDNN: cuDNN version mismatch: expected 8300, found 7610
```
Theo: building with `make -j6 BUILD_USE_CUDA=1` inside a docker container launched with `--gpus all` from WSL distro
Mika: welcome! WSL adds a layer of oddness. first, confirm host driver (Windows side) `nvidia-smi` in PowerShell and `nvidia-smi` inside WSL - they should agree. WSL driver must be modern (>=525 for CUDA 11.8).
Eli: also check the container image toolkit vs host driver. The PTX unsupported error usually means the container's nvcc/ptxas generated PTX newer than the host NVIDIA driver understands. In WSL the Windows driver is used for runtime.
Samir: for the cuDNN ABI mismatch, check which cuDNN package the container provides. Many distro packages install cuDNN8.3 vs 7.6. We pin runtime to the cuDNN expected by our binaries. What does `ldd` show on the built binary?
Theo: host `nvidia-smi` -> Driver 520.61, inside WSL same. container `ptxas --version` -> 10.6.0; cuDNN in container shows 7.6 via `cat /usr/include/cudnn_version.h` but our repo expects 8.3 per cmake logs
Mika: driver 520 is probably the root cause for PTX 8.7. Two options: (1) point your build to a toolkit that emits older PTX (set TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST to supported SMs) or (2) upgrade Windows driver to 525+. For cuDNN, align container image to cuDNN 8.3 or adjust build flags to avoid APIs that require 8.3.
Eli: quick WSL tip: avoid mixing toolkit versions between host and container. If you must build inside container, use an image matching host driver ABI (we have registry images tagged for WSL). infra-bot: list recommended images.
infra-bot: Recommended WSL-friendly dev image: registry.redwood/internal/runtime-dev:cuda11.8-wsl-gcc12-2026-03-15 (cuDNN 8.3, driver compatibility 525+). CI GPU runners: driver 525.85+.
Theo: can't upgrade Windows driver right now (company policy). is there a local build workaround?
Samir: set `export TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=\"7.5;7.0;6.1\"` and add `export CUDA_NVCC_FLAGS=\"-gencode arch=compute_70,code=sm_70\"` before make. That prevents nvcc emitting PTX for newer archs. Also for cuDNN mismatch, you can build against cuDNN headers available but runtime may fail if host lacks symbols. For tests that don't actually execute GPU kernels, stub them or run CPU-only tests locally.
Theo: tried TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST and build proceeds past ptxas. Now at test run I get runtime symbol error: `undefined symbol: cudnnGetVersion` when invoking GPU smoke test inside container (even though header matched)
Eli: runtime symbol missing confirms host-side driver/cuda libs (via WSL) don't expose the newer cuDNN symbols. In WSL the Windows driver provides CUDA drivers; cuDNN is userland in the container. If the binary links to a version that expects newer driver-side symbols, you'll see that. Best practice: for dev on corp-managed Windows, build artifacts in container but run GPU tests on infra GPUs (VMs or CI) with drivers 525+.
Mika: adding to onboarding checklist: 1) verify Windows host driver >=525 for WSL CUDA 11.8; 2) use our WSL-friendly dev image if possible; 3) when driver upgrade impossible, use TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST fallback + run GPU tests on infra; 4) ensure cuDNN packages in image match repo expectations; 5) LD_LIBRARY_PATH or rpath if container complains.
Theo: noted. one more quirky thing: docker container shows `/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcudnn.so.8 -> libcuDNN-8.3.1.so` but ldd on binary inside container still lists `libcudnn.so.8 => not found` until I export LD_LIBRARY_PATH. Is that expected?
Samir: yes, inside container you need LD_LIBRARY_PATH pointing to the location or build with `-Wl,-rpath,/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu`. Also confirm container user has permissions to access mounted driver files from WSL.
Theo: okay thanks. i'll document the WSL-specific notes and open a small PR to eng-runtime onboarding: WSL checks, recommended image tag, TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST tip, and rpath/LD_LIBRARY_PATH steps. appreciate the help!
Mika: great, ping me for review. welcome to the team Theo :wave:
Theo: thanks everyone :tada:
